Feasible GLS for serial correlation and/or heteroskedasticity

Source: R/fgls.R
fgls.Rd

fgls() fits a linear regression by feasible generalized least squares, correcting for serially correlated errors (Perron and González-Coya, 2026), for heteroskedasticity of unknown form (González-Coya and Perron, 2024), or for both (the "F-CH" estimator of Supplement S-4 of the 2026 paper). serial_fgls() and lasso_fgls() are shortcuts for the two single corrections.

Usage

fgls(
  formula,
  data,
  subset,
  na.action = stats::na.fail,
  serial = c("auto", "fixed", "ma1", "none"),
  hetero = c("lasso", "svr", "wls_s1", "wls_s2", "known", "none"),
  vcov = c("robust", "naive", "nonrobust", "HC0", "HC1", "HC2", "HC3", "bootstrap"),
  z = "auto",
  ar_order = NULL,
  kmax = NULL,
  ic = c("bic", "aic"),
  lagged_dep_vars = NULL,
  wallis_regressor = "auto",
  exog = c("predetermined", "exogenous"),
  first_stage_correction = NULL,
  variance = NULL,
  delta = 0.1,
  psi_grid = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 2),
  cv_folds = 10L,
  lambda_rule = c("min", "1se"),
  weight_clip = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  use_t = FALSE,
  time = NULL,
  allow_gaps = FALSE,
  check_stationarity = FALSE,
  control = fgls_control(),
  contrasts = NULL,
  model = TRUE,
  weights,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula

A model formula, as in stats::lm(). Include an intercept unless the model truly has none.

data

A data frame, a list, a ts/mts object, or a 'zoo'/'xts' object containing the variables in the formula. Rows must be in time order (unless serial = "none").

subset

Optional expression selecting rows, evaluated in data. For time series without a time index (time, or a ts/zoo data) the selected rows must be an increasing block of consecutive rows (e.g. subset = 51:200): repeated or reversed rows are an error, and so are skipped rows unless allow_gaps = TRUE.

na.action

stats::na.fail() (default) stops on missing values; stats::na.omit() or stats::na.exclude() drop them. For time series only leading and trailing missing values can be dropped. With na.exclude, residuals() and fitted() are padded with NA to the rows selected by subset, as for stats::lm().

serial

Serial-correlation correction: "auto" (AR order by BIC, default), "fixed" (use ar_order), "ma1" (GMA for MA(1) errors; it does not take ar_order, kmax or lagged_dep_vars) or "none".

hetero

Skedastic-function estimator: "lasso" (adaptive Lasso, default), "svr" (support vector regression, requires 'e1071'), "wls_s1"/"wls_s2" (the parametric fits of Romano and Wolf, 2017, on \(\log z\) or \(z\)), "known" (variances given in variance) or "none". "wls_s1" takes logs, so it needs strictly positive candidate covariates given explicitly in z (e.g. z = "x" for a positive regressor x); the cosine terms of the default z = "auto" are usually negative somewhere, which is an error.

vcov

Variance estimator; the default "robust" is PG26 eq. (29) with the serial correction only, GP24 eqs. (6) and (8) with the heteroskedasticity correction only, and Supplement eqs. (A.4)–(A.5) with both. The types available depend on the corrections:

  • serial only (hetero = "none"): "robust", "naive" (PG26 eq. 27, exogenous regressors only), "HC0"–"HC3" and "bootstrap" (sieve bootstrap); with serial = "ma1" only "robust";

  • heteroskedasticity only (serial = "none"): "robust", "nonrobust", "HC0"–"HC3" and "bootstrap" (wild bootstrap);

  • both (the default): "robust", "HC0", "HC3" and "bootstrap" (sieve bootstrap).

Any other choice is an error. See vcov.fgls().

z

Candidate covariates of the skedastic function: "auto" (default) builds \(\{x, x^2, \log x, (\log x)^2, \cos x, \cos 2x\}\) from every non-constant regressor (see make_dictionary()); a character vector of regressor names; a one-sided formula evaluated in data (e.g. ~ x + I(x^2) + w); or a numeric matrix / data frame with one row per row of data. With hetero = "wls_s1" all candidates must be strictly positive, so give them explicitly, e.g. z = "x" or z = ~ x + I(x^2) for a positive regressor x.

ar_order

Fixed AR order (implies serial = "fixed").

kmax

Largest AR order considered: NULL (default, \(\lfloor 12 (T/200)^{1/4} \rfloor\)), an integer, or "theory" (\(\lfloor (T/\ln T)^{1/3} \rfloor\)). It is capped so that the Durbin regression uses at most half of the sample as regressors.

ic

Lag-order criterion: "bic" (default) or "aic".

lagged_dep_vars

Names (or positions) of model-matrix columns that are lags of the dependent variable (not available with serial = "ma1").

wallis_regressor

Regressor used for the Wallis recovery of the AR coefficients: "auto" (largest Durbin \(|t|\)), "median", or a name.

exog

Assumption on the regressors: "predetermined" (default) or "exogenous". Estimates do not depend on it; it sets the default of first_stage_correction and the notes of the summary.

first_stage_correction

Add the first-stage (Durbin) term of PG26 eq. (29) to the variance of the combined estimator. Default TRUE when exog = "predetermined".

variance

Known error variances for hetero = "known": a numeric vector with one value per row of data, whose values are selected by subset and na.action together with the rows of the data (a vector with one value per observation used is also accepted); or a function of the model matrix returning one value per observation used.

delta

Floor in \(\log\max(\hat u_t^2, \delta^2)\), in the units of the response (default 0.1, as in the paper).

psi_grid

Exponents \(\psi\) of the adaptive weights; 0 is the plain Lasso.

cv_folds

Number of cross-validation folds (default 10).

lambda_rule

Penalty at the minimum of the cross-validation error ("min", default) or the largest penalty within one standard error of it ("1se").

weight_clip

Optional quantiles c(lo, hi) at which the fitted log-variance is winsorized, e.g. c(0.01, 0.99).

seed

Optional seed for the cross-validation folds and the bootstrap. The session's random number generator state is restored afterwards.

use_t

Use Student-t (n_eff - q degrees of freedom) instead of normal inference.

time

Time index for data frames: the name of a Date, POSIXct or numeric column of data, or a vector with one value per row. It is used to check that rows are sorted and have no gaps, and must have no missing values in the sample. Convert character dates first, e.g. with as.Date() or zoo::as.yearmon().

allow_gaps

Accept a time index with gaps, or a subset that skips rows (lags are then positional), with a warning.

check_stationarity

Screen the response and the regressors with augmented Dickey-Fuller tests and warn when a unit root is not rejected.

control

Advanced options, see fgls_control().

contrasts

Optional list of contrasts for factors, as in stats::lm().

model

Keep the model frame in the result.

weights

Not supported: FGLS estimates its own weights. Use hetero = "known" with variance for known variances.

...

Not used; unknown arguments are an error.

Value

An object of class "fgls", a list with components including

coefficients, vcov

Estimates and their covariance matrix.

residuals, fitted.values

\(y_t - x_t'\hat\beta\) and \(x_t'\hat\beta\) on the full sample.

innovations

Residuals of the final (filtered and/or weighted) regression.

ar_order, rho, bic_path, nonexogeneity_share

Serial block (NULL without serial correction); more in serial.

skedastic, weights

Heteroskedasticity block: selected covariates, coefficients, \(\psi\), \(\lambda\), degrees of freedom, fitted variances; weights are \(1/\hat v_t\). For the Lasso, skedastic$lambda is the selected penalty on the scale of 'glmnet', whose objective is that of GP24 eq. (4) divided by the number of observations \(n\) of the skedastic regression, and skedastic$lambda_paper \(= n \lambda\) is the same penalty on the scale of eq. (4). Both refer to the standardized candidate covariates.

stages

Intermediate estimators (stages$serial is F-C). They are "fgls" objects with the same methods as the final fit; vcov(fit$stages$serial, type =) accepts "robust", "HC0" and "HC3".

nobs, n_eff

Number of observations and of observations in the final regression (\(T - k^*\)).

Use the methods summary(), coef(), vcov(), confint(), predict(), residuals(), plot() and compare_fgls().

Serial correlation (PG26)

The errors are approximated by an AR(k) process. Its coefficients are the coefficients on the lagged dependent variable in the Durbin regression of \(y_t\) on \(y_{t-1}, \dots, y_{t-k}\), \(x_t, \dots, x_{t-k}\) (eq. 14), and \(k\) is chosen by BIC over \(0, \dots, k_{max}\) on a common sample. The data are then quasi-differenced and the model is estimated by OLS on the filtered data (eq. 15), dropping the first \(k\) observations. Unlike Cochrane-Orcutt, this is consistent when the regressors are only pre-determined (uncorrelated with current and future innovations) rather than strictly exogenous. The default variance (vcov = "robust", eqs. 28–29) accounts for the estimation of the filter and is valid in both cases; vcov = "naive" (eq. 27) is valid only for exogenous regressors. The share by which the robust variance exceeds the naive one is reported as nonexogeneity_share. If the selected order is 0, FGLS equals OLS.

Heteroskedasticity (GP24)

The log of the squared OLS residuals (floored at delta^2) is regressed on candidate covariates \(z_t\) by an adaptive Lasso: a ridge first step gives weights \(|\hat\gamma_j|^{-\psi}\), and the penalty \(\lambda\) and the exponent \(\psi\) are chosen jointly by 10-fold cross-validation with the same folds for every \(\psi\). The exponentiated fit gives the weights of a weighted least-squares regression. Inference uses a sandwich variance with the bias correction of eq. (8), so it stays valid when the skedastic model is wrong. If the Lasso selects no covariate the weights are constant and FGLS equals OLS (no loss under homoskedasticity).

Both (Supplement S-4)

With serial != "none" and hetero != "none" the serial correction is applied first ("F-C"), the skedastic function is fitted to the residuals of the quasi-differenced regression with candidate covariates built from the unfiltered regressors, and the quasi-differenced regression is re-estimated by weighted least squares ("F-CH"). The F-C stage is kept in fit$stages$serial.

Choosing options

  • Time series with possibly autocorrelated errors and no concern about heteroskedasticity: hetero = "none" (or serial_fgls()).

  • Cross-sectional data: serial = "none" (or lasso_fgls()). Rows can be in any order.

  • Lagged dependent variables among the regressors must be declared in lagged_dep_vars; the AR coefficients are then recovered by the Wallis ratio (PG26 Section 4.2).

  • Errors known to be MA(1), e.g. multi-step forecast errors: serial = "ma1" (GMA estimator, PG26 Section 5).

  • With several stochastic regressors the BIC that penalizes only the AR order can select kmax; use control = fgls_control(ic_penalty = "params").

  • Results involving cross-validation depend on the random folds: set seed for reproducibility.

References

Perron, P. and González-Coya, E. (2026). Feasible GLS for time series regression. Journal of Econometrics, 258, 106346. doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2026.106346

González-Coya, E. and Perron, P. (2024). Estimation in the presence of heteroskedasticity of unknown form: a Lasso-based approach. Journal of Econometric Methods, 13(1), 29–48. doi:10.1515/jem-2023-0007

Romano, J. P. and Wolf, M. (2017). Resurrecting weighted least squares. Journal of Econometrics, 197(1), 1–19. doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2016.10.003

Examples

# Serial correlation with a non-exogenous regressor (PG26 Table 1 design)
sim <- simulate_serial(300, seed = 1)
fit <- fgls(y ~ x, data = sim, hetero = "none")
summary(fit)
#> 
#> Call:
#> fgls(formula = y ~ x, data = sim, hetero = "none")
#> 
#> Method:               FGLS (serial)
#> Covariance:           robust
#> Observations:         300 (effective 299)
#> Inference:            normal
#> AR order k*:          1 [BIC, kmax = 13]
#> AR coefficients:      0.7654
#> Non-exogeneity share: 0.012
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> (Intercept)  1.18739    0.23736   5.002 5.66e-07 ***
#> x            0.98640    0.03202  30.809  < 2e-16 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Notes:
#> [1] Covariance: PG26 eq. (29), robust to non-exogenous (pre-determined)
#>     regressors.
#> [2] Collinear lagged columns dropped from the Durbin regression:
#>     L1.(Intercept).
#> 

# Heteroskedasticity of unknown form (GP24)
het <- simulate_hetero(200, skedastic = "log2", seed = 2)
fit2 <- fgls(y ~ x, data = het, serial = "none", seed = 1)
fit2$skedastic$selected
#> [1] "log(x)" "cos(x)"

# Both (Supplement S-4)
both <- simulate_combined(200, ar = 0.5, skedastic = "x2", seed = 3)
fit3 <- fgls(y ~ x, data = both, seed = 1)
compare_fgls(fit3$stages$serial, fit3)
#>          term statistic F-C (serial) F-CH (serial+hetero)
#> 1 (Intercept)  estimate    1.3723275            1.5934094
#> 2 (Intercept) std.error    0.5413481            0.4430785
#> 3 (Intercept)  ci.width    2.1220455            1.7368357
#> 4           x  estimate    0.9130718            0.8100948
#> 5           x std.error    0.2611294            0.2123379
#> 6           x  ci.width    1.0236086            0.8323494
